speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're having trouble walking and pointing to a specific spot that hurts. Can you tell me exactly where the pain is located, and does it hurt more when you put weight on that leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the pain is in the knee but the child favors the left leg, could you tell me if he ever complains of pain in his hip or buttock, even if he points to his knee? Also, does the pain wake him up at night or occur at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE).

Although the pain is referred to the knee, the combination of a limp, hip/buttock referral pain (often missed), and lack of trauma in an obese or growing child is classic for SCFE. Given the high suspicion, I request an X-RAY of the left hip AP and Frog-leg lateral views immediately.
